app.title: fraud_screen: numerical anomaly screening of paper source data
app.summary: A person uploads a paper's source-data spreadsheets, CSVs, PDFs or a ZIP, or generates a synthetic demo paper. They can also list target figures or panels and add a case note. They start the screening and watch a live log of stages, files, sheets, records extracted and flags found, and they can cancel the run. The results show a risk score and level, flag counts by severity and by review priority, and the top 20 flags ranked for manual review. The person then downloads the HTML, JSON, CSV and Markdown reports, a run manifest with input and configuration hashes, or one ZIP with everything.

task.text: Screen the numerical source data behind a paper's figures for suspicious patterns and produce a prioritised list of what a person should review by hand.

data.text: Tables of numbers behind a paper's figures, read sheet by sheet into records of figure, panel, group, x label, value, SD, SEM and n, plus the anomaly flags computed from them, each with risk points and a priority.
data.item: a vector of values from one panel of a figure's source-data sheet

stage.text: screening published source data for anomalies, before manual integrity review

mechanism.text: Settings in a sidebar and an upload area feed a batch screening run that reports its progress live. When it finishes, a results dashboard of metric cards, a risk-level verdict and a ranked table of the top flags sits above a grid of download buttons for every report file.

field.text: statistical forensics of figure source data in research integrity review

workflow.name: screen a set of data tables for suspicious patterns and rank them for manual review

steps.here: Upload Excel, CSV, PDF or ZIP files under a paper ID (ZIPs are unpacked), or click Run built-in demo to generate a synthetic paper

steps.step: say which items matter before the run
steps.here: Optionally list target figures or panels and write a case note about known concerns, and choose aggressive mode, the reviewer report and a threshold config file

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Start screening reads every sheet into records and runs the detectors. A progress bar and activity log show the stage, the current file and sheet, records extracted, flags found and elapsed time, and Cancel stops after the current phase

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: Metric cards show the risk score and level, the number of anomaly flags, High/Med/Low and P1/P2/P3 counts, an overall verdict and how many sheets were skipped

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A table shows the 20 flags with the most risk points, with priority, severity, detector, figure, evidence and recommended action

Download buttons give the HTML report, JSON, anomaly CSV, review queue, quality report, target-figure review, case review CSV and Markdown, manifest, metadata and performance log, or one ZIP. A panel shows the run's fingerprint and config hashes

distinctive: A set of detectors looks for patterns that suggest fabricated numbers: exact and rounded duplicate vectors, constant offsets and ratios, near-perfect linear fits, SEM/SD/n inconsistency, repeated error values, terminal-digit and Benford first-digit tests, and overly smooth trends
Each flag carries risk points that set its review priority: P1 at 30 or more, P2 at 15 or more, P3 below that. The paper's total score maps to risk levels 0 to 4
Target figures named from a case note or retraction notice are matched against the sheet inventory and the flags, and each is reported as found with flags, found without flags, or not found
Each run records the input file hashes, an input fingerprint, and config and detector-config hashes, so its results can be traced and reproduced
Every report says that a statistical anomaly is not evidence of misconduct and that a clean result does not prove the data are authentic
